name: get_routine_detail
description: Fetch one routine's FULL if/then/else automation logic -- real device/routine/variable ids, uom values, and the same GE/GT/IS/ISNOT/LE/LT-style op tokens and status/control/schedule/cmd/etc field shapes documented in create_or_update_routine's description (use that grammar to interpret this tool's result and explain it in plain language). Any value whose uom is an index/enum type (25/146/148) is annotated with a real `label` string alongside the raw `value` (resolved from the actual device/command/property, not guessed) -- always prefer and relay `label` over the raw number when explaining a routine to the customer; if a value has no `label`, it's a plain number, not an unresolved enum. A `var` node also gets a real `name` resolved onto it. CRITICAL: a `var` node in `if` is always a COMPARISON (op is one of GT/GE/LT/LE/IS/ISNOT) -- describe it as a check. A `var` node in `then`/`else` is always an ASSIGNMENT (op is one of EQ/ADD=/SUB=/MUL=/DIV=/REM=/AND=/OR=/XOR=/RDM=/INIT), never a check, even though EQ reads like the English word "equals" -- it gets an `op_label` (e.g. "set equal to", "increase by") annotated onto it; always describe it using that label (e.g. "sets Watering_the_plants to 1"), never as "checks if ... equals". ROUTINES DATABASE only lists a routine's name/comment/referenced devices/referenced variables, never its actual logic -- call this tool for any 'what does this routine do', 'show me the full logic', or 'explain this routine' question, and before editing an existing routine's logic with create_or_update_routine.

id.description: Real routine id, exactly as shown in ROUTINES DATABASE.
